docs/rebuild/s15/builds/Q — index.html (lines 96–142 hold the whole signature) and design-plan.md (§Signatur, §Kritik af planen, §Risikoen jeg tager). Compared against docs/rebuild/s15/builds/P/index.html (.kanal at lines 170–199, .rulle SVG at 635–676) and P/.sitesmith/direction.md (§Signature, §Imagery treatment). Skill surfaces read in full: skills/sitesmith-v3/SKILL.md, verify.md, run.md, floor/buy.md.

HOW THE ROLL IS ACTUALLY BUILT (technique, not appearance)

The band is a flex column of ten sibling divs (.spor), flex:1 1 0, so they cut the band into ten equal lanes. Each lane carries linear-gradient(90deg, var(--stops)) where --stops is a per-lane list of HARD stops (transparent 0 24px, ink 24px 38px, transparent 38px 132px, ...). Hard stops mean no interpolation, so the gradient is a step function that renders rectangles, not a blur. background-size:320px 100% with background-repeat:repeat makes every lane tile the same 320px period. padding:5px 0 plus background-clip:content-box leaves an unpainted gutter at the top and bottom of each lane, which is what stops adjacent holes from fusing into vertical stripes; the perforations read as discrete punched rows. The animation moves background-position-x from 0 to -320px over 10s linear infinite: the travel distance equals the tile period exactly, so the loop is seamless with no seam arithmetic and no JS. Because the ten lanes share the period but not the stop list, they never phase-align, so the eye sees an aperiodic hole field built from ten individually periodic lanes.

Two flat overlays then supply the physics. .rulle::after is an absolutely positioned inset:0 layer with a 180deg four-stop gradient (dark at 0, transparent 22% to 76%, dark at the bottom): that is the paper curling away at both edges, and it is what turns a pattern into a cylinder. .trackerbar is 17px wide, absolutely positioned with top:-12px;bottom:-12px so it OVERHANGS the band at both ends and therefore sits in front of the paper rather than inside it. Its face is a four-stop 90deg gradient with the highlight off-centre at 38%, which is what makes a flat rectangle read as round metal; box-shadow gives it a 1.5px containment ring plus a 9px 0 18px cast shadow thrown in ONE direction only, so the light has a stated side. Its ::after is inset:16px 4px with repeating-linear-gradient(180deg, near-black 0 5px, transparent 5px 10%) for the row of ports down the face.

The band is also outside .wrap, so it is full-bleed at clamp(150px,20vw,222px) tall directly under the hero, and only the note beneath it is width-constrained. The still reprise later on the page is the same markup with .rulle--stille and .spor:nth-child(n+7){display:none} — six lanes, no second asset.

WHY IT READS AS THE OBJECT AND OURS NEEDED A CAPTION

Four causes, in order of weight.

1. It draws the counterpart. The perforated field alone is a texture. The brass bar crossing it, overhanging it, shadowed on one side, ported down its face, is the part that CONSUMES the paper. Material plus the thing acting on the material is a mechanism; material alone is wallpaper. Our roll is drawn without its trakterstang, in a section (E) that is not the section where the trakterstang is explained (B).

2. It is lit, and ours is not. Q has two lit surfaces (paper curvature, off-centre specular on metal) and one consistent light direction. P has --kanalfyld, a three-stop 90deg gradient at .17/.05/.15 between two 2px brass borders — the same class of trick, executed correctly, at 18px wide in the left gutter where it can only read as a rule. P even needs .kanal--start and .kanal--slut caps to tell the reader it is a pipe. Nothing else on P is lit at all.

3. Scale and register. Q's object is full-bleed and 150–222px tall, at the size the object is relative to a person. P's roll is an SVG at max-width:122px in a margin column.

4. The caption asymmetry is the tell, and it points at fidelity. Q's line under the band ("Papir, huller, messing og luft — det er hele mekanikken") ADDS a fact. P's line under the SVG ("Skematisk tegning af en perforeret rulle. Ikke en bestemt titel og ikke en måltegning") DEFENDS the drawing's accuracy. A drawn artefact that needs a disclaimer is drawn at the wrong fidelity: it is detailed enough to be read as a measurement and not physical enough to be read as an object. Either draw it as an object or draw it as unmistakable linework. The disclaimer is the diagnostic.

WHAT Q'S PLAN DOES AT THE POINT OF CHOOSING A SIGNATURE THAT OURS DOES NOT

Q's §Signatur is 6 lines and half of it is construction: "Ren CSS: ti linear-gradient-spor med hver sin stopliste over en 240px-periode, animeret på background-position-x. Slukkes ved prefers-reduced-motion. Rullen optræder én gang mere, stillestående." Elements, the repeating unit, the one property that changes, the reduced-motion behaviour, and the dosage — before code.

P's §Signature is three paragraphs and none of it is construction. It says what the channel MEANS (following the vacuum from bellows to striker), names its kind against three near-misses ("ikke en vandret måler, ikke en trinbjælke, ikke et ikonsæt"), and answers the swap test ("fem kort ville påstå fem uafhængige problemer, og det er forkert"). Every one of those is SKILL.md §6 working as written. But because the field never says how the thing is drawn, the build drew the cheapest thing that satisfies the prose: two borders and a fill. The drawing budget then leaked to a 122px SVG in another section. That is the causal chain, and it is upstream of anything verify.md can catch.

Q's plan also carries two fields ours has no equivalent of. §Risikoen jeg tager defends the DEVICE, not the page: it names the failure mode the device is nearest to (an infinite ambient hero loop is normally motion without a reason) and then states the parameters that keep it on the right side (low speed, low contrast, stops dead at prefers-reduced-motion). P's §Risk describes the page's posture instead — leads with faults, red only for damage, no photography — which is a stance, not a defence. And Q's §Kritik point 4 states the dosage explicitly and names the ornament removed to protect it: perforated page edges cut, "rullen skal være ét sted, ellers er den tapet". P instead ran its signature down the left edge of every single section, which is arguably the exact failure Q named and deleted.

techniques.name: Draw the counterpart, not the material
techniques.howItIsBuilt: The signature is two parts with different jobs: the medium (ten gradient lanes of perforated paper) and the fixed thing acting on it (the tracker bar, overhanging the band top and bottom so it sits in front, shadowed in one direction, ported down its face). Neither half is the signature. Q's roll needs no explanation because the reader can see what eats the paper. Our roll SVG has no trakterstang across it and is filed in a different section from where the trakterstang is explained, so it can only be a picture of a thing.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: This is the whole gap between 'best single hero device in the set' and a 122px thumbnail carrying a disclaimer. P's direction record names its signature's kind correctly and argues the swap test correctly, and still shipped a texture with no counterpart, because nothing in the package asks for the second part. It also generalises with no convergence pressure at all: punch card under a reader, film under a gate, cloth under a needle bar, seed tape under a coulter, ledger under a rule and a nib. The counterpart is always different because the trade is.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Rewrite verify.md render question 3 in place. Current: '**Is the signature visible at 1440 and alive at 375?** One that exists only in the design record is not a signature.' Proposed: '**Name the signature's two parts, the material and the thing acting on it.** A texture with no counterpart drawn is wallpaper; one that lives only in the design record is not a signature; and one that needs a caption to be identified is drawn at the wrong fidelity, so either light it or reduce it to linework.' Displacement, since verify.md is at 4,599 of 4,600: delete the trailing justification in the report contract, 'An absent field is detectable where an absent behaviour is invisible, which is the entire reason the block is fixed rather than written to taste.' (144 chars, ~36 tokens). The rule it justifies, 'A missing field, or a missing reason on a step that did not run, fails the gate', is stated immediately before it and survives intact.
techniques.risk: Low. It adds no look and cannot make briefs converge, because the counterpart is drawn from section 3 nouns and is different in every trade. The one failure mode is a build answering the question in prose without drawing anything, which is the same failure the question already catches for the signature itself.

techniques.name: The signature field states a construction, not only a meaning
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Q's plan specifies the device before code as elements, repeating unit, the one property that is animated, and the reduced-motion behaviour: ten gradient lanes, one shared period, background-position-x, off at prefers-reduced-motion. P's plan specifies meaning, kind and consequence and no drawing method, and the build then produced the minimum reading of that prose. Q's own plan/code divergence proves the field is a spec and not a decoration: the plan says 240px and 8s, the code ships 320px and 10s, because a spec is a thing you tune and prose is not.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: This is the single point where our loss is upstream of every check we own. SKILL.md §6 asks for the signature's kind, its cost if swapped, and one risk — all evaluative, all satisfiable without deciding how anything is drawn. Nothing in SKILL.md, run.md or verify.md ever asks how the mark is made, so the cheapest construction that matches the sentence always wins, and it did.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Two sentences appended to the Signature block of SKILL.md §6: 'State how it is drawn: the elements, the unit that repeats, the one property that changes and the one that must not. A signature described only by what it means gets built as the cheapest thing that satisfies the description.' (~225 chars, ~56 tokens). Enforcement is not the prose: ledger.mjs owns the direction-record heading list and already fails a blank heading, so it gains a refusal when the Signature section contains no construction noun (element, gradient, stroke, grid, mask, transform, property). Displacement, both in §6 and §5, since always is at 3,095 of 3,100: (a) collapse the colour-paragraph evidence, 'Three briefs each produced four to six well named values and each landed on the same five jobs: light ground, lighter surface, near black ink, one saturated accent, desaturated secondary.' plus 'The names diverged and the roles did not, because asking what each colour is *for* answers with the same list every time.' (305 chars) into 'Three briefs did this and each landed on the same five jobs, because asking what a colour is *for* answers with the same list every time.' (135 chars), saving ~43 tokens; (b) delete §5's restatement 'Naming defaults moves the work to the next unnamed one.' (54 chars, ~14 tokens), whose content is carried by the sentence before it. Net change to the always surface: roughly minus 1 token.
techniques.target: skills/sitesmith-v3/SKILL.md §6 Signature, plus a refusal in scripts/ledger.mjs
techniques.risk: Low to medium. The risk is that a construction line becomes a recipe line and three briefs copy it, so the field must be checked for BEING a construction and never for MATCHING one. ledger.mjs may only refuse an empty field; it may not compare constructions across builds, or it becomes a script deciding a design.

techniques.name: One stated light direction, then two flat overlays carry the physics
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Two overlays, both flat CSS, both subject-neutral. Curvature: a perpendicular multi-stop gradient over the whole surface, dark at both ends and transparent across the middle (Q: 180deg, .16 at 0, transparent 22–76%, .18 at the bottom), which reads as the surface turning away from the viewer. Specular: on a metal or glossy part, a highlight stop placed OFF centre (Q: 38% of a four-stop 90deg gradient) plus a cast shadow thrown one way only (9px 0 18px, positive x, no negative), plus a hairline containment ring. Both derive from one light direction, stated once and obeyed everywhere.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P has no lit surface anywhere on the page. Its --kanalfyld shows the instinct is present and correct (a 90deg three-stop gradient IS a cylinder seen from the side) but at 18px in a gutter there is nothing for it to be a cylinder of. Lighting is why Q's band identifies itself without a caption, and it produces a different result per subject: leather, enamel, glass, wet slate and a stone sill each want different stop counts and positions from the same rule.
techniques.sitesmithForm: A new conditional reference, skills/sitesmith-v3/craft/surface.md, opened at run.md build step 6 only when the direction record's Signature field names a drawn object — the same conditional-open shape stacks/* already uses, so it costs nothing against the always ceiling and nothing against routine on runs whose signature is typographic or structural. Contents: the light-direction rule (state it once in the direction record, in words, and never contradict it), the curvature overlay, the off-centre specular plus one-directional cast shadow, and the standing refusal that shadows may not point in more than one direction on a page, which is one of the most reliable AI-look tells and is currently unchecked anywhere in the package.
techniques.target: new skills/sitesmith-v3/craft/surface.md, referenced from run.md step 6
techniques.risk: Medium, and this is the one to watch. Written as a recipe it is a skeuomorph kit and three briefs converge on shaded plates. It survives only as a physics constraint keyed to a light direction the build states for itself, with the file naming no material and no hex value. If it cannot be written that way it should not be written.

techniques.name: Signature dosage: once loud, once quiet, and one ornament deleted to protect it
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Q decides the device's dosage in the plan rather than in the build. It appears twice and only twice: full-bleed and moving under the hero, then again small, still and six lanes deep in the section about rolls, reusing the same markup via nth-child(n+7){display:none}. And §Kritik point 4 records the thing removed to keep it rare: perforated page edges down both margins, cut because 'rullen skal være ét sted, ellers er den tapet'.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P ran its signature down the left edge of every section from header to footer. That is argued in P's plan as the air path and it is not wrong, but it converts the signature into a page frame, and a frame is furniture. Q names the exact failure and pays a specific ornament to avoid it. SKILL.md §6 gestures at this once ('Spend your boldness here and keep everything around it quiet') without ever asking how many times the thing appears or what was cut for it, and neither the plan nor any check records the answer.
techniques.sitesmithForm: A heading in the direction record, owned by scripts/ledger.mjs, not prose in SKILL.md: 'Dosage: where the signature appears, how many times, and the one thing removed so it stays rare.' Blank-heading refusal already exists in ledger.mjs, so enforcement is free. Cost lands on the build's written record, not on any skill ceiling.
techniques.risk: Low. It fights convergence rather than causing it, since the ornament removed is different per subject. Mild risk of becoming a ritual sacrifice where a build invents an ornament in order to delete it, which the render questions would not catch.

techniques.name: One tiling period, N phased lanes, one animated property
techniques.howItIsBuilt: N sibling elements divide a band, all sharing one background-size period and one background-repeat, each with its own hard-stop gradient so no two phase-align; padding plus background-clip:content-box keeps neighbouring lanes from fusing; the only animated property is background-position, and the travel distance equals the period exactly so the loop is seamless with no JS and no seam maths. The aperiodic result is an emergent property of N periodic lanes, not of any lane being complex.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P has no repeating-field technique at all, and its one field of marks is 30 hand-placed SVG rects that cannot be re-timed, re-scaled or reused. The lane structure is genuinely general: it renders any medium that carries discrete marks across a fixed head, and it degrades to a static field by simply not animating, which matters because floor/buy.md forbids motion near money and P's whole no-motion stance follows from that.
techniques.sitesmithForm: The structural half only, as one line inside craft/surface.md: N lanes, one shared period, per-lane phase, one animated property, travel equals period. It must be written with no stop values, no lane count and no duration, or it becomes the recipe. It is not proposed for SKILL.md, run.md or verify.md at any price.
techniques.risk: High if written with numbers, low if written as structure. This is the item most likely to make three unrelated briefs converge, because 'animated repeating strip in the hero' is a shape a model reaches for readily. It is worth carrying only because item 1 gates it: a lane field with no counterpart drawn is refused as wallpaper before it can become a house style.

techniques.name: Substitute the marker, do not only cut it
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Q's §Kritik point 1 keeps the marker slot in the four-step sequence and changes what fills it. 01/02/03 is removed, but the slot survives as DU / VI / DU / DU, on the argument that the reader is not missing the order, they are missing who acts. The five faults get the same treatment: their eyebrow is the fault itself, SMULDRET / REVNET / SLIDT / SPRUKKET / HÅRDE, not an index.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P did cut correctly — its direction record says 01/02/03 steps were removed because the brief does not state a restoration order — and then filled the remaining slots with A to F and 1 to 5, which is exactly the index Q rejected. SKILL.md §6 currently instructs 'ask what each device claims, and cut the ones that claim nothing', which authorises deletion and is silent on substitution, so a build that keeps a slot has no guidance for what to put in it.
techniques.sitesmithForm: One clause edited into SKILL.md §6 Structure: change 'and cut the ones that claim nothing' to 'cut the ones that claim nothing, and where a slot must stay, fill it with the dimension the reader actually lacks: who acts, not what order.' (+105 chars, ~26 tokens). Displacement inside the same paragraph: delete the now-redundant example '`01/02/03` claims the content is ordered.' (41 chars, ~10 tokens), whose content the new clause carries. Net roughly +16 tokens against the always ceiling, on top of the net minus 1 from item 2, so both fit together.
techniques.risk: Low. Mild risk that 'who acts' becomes the substitution every build reaches for, which is why the clause should name it as an example of a dimension rather than as the dimension.

techniques.name: One variable axis mapped to one semantic ladder
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Q loads Archivo with its width axis (wdth 100..125) and never uses it decoratively. Width climbs with how much an element is a nameplate: body and secondary spans at 100, section headings and list items at 110, buttons at 112, stat values at 114, h1 and h2 at 116, the workshop name and the largest numerals at 120. Size and width move together as one ladder, so a heading is not merely bigger, it is a wider cut of the same face.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P uses three static faces with static weights, which is defensible, but it means every type decision is size and weight only. The technique carries to any variable axis, wdth, opsz, slnt or GRAD, and produces a different result per face, so it does not converge. It is the smallest item here and the judges specifically noticed it, which is worth knowing about how a single axis used with intent reads.
techniques.sitesmithForm: One line in the type section of craft/surface.md, not in SKILL.md: if a face has a variable axis, map it to one semantic ladder and say which axis and which ladder in the direction record; an axis set per element is decoration. It does not fit the always surface at any honest displacement, so it should not go there.
techniques.risk: Low, but it is also the item most likely to be ignored, since it is advice with no check behind it. There is no cheap way to verify a ladder from a render, so it stays guidance and should be labelled as such.

found.whatOursLacks:
Three concrete absences in P, in causal order.

1. The direction record's Signature field contains no construction. It is 22 lines across three paragraphs: what the channel means (following the vacuum from bellows to striker), its kind and three near-misses it is explicitly not, and the swap-test answer. All correct by SKILL.md §6 as written, and none of it says how the thing is drawn. The build then produced the minimum that satisfies the sentence: .kanal is two 2px borders, a three-stop fill and two 3px caps, 18px wide in a 56px gutter. The drawing budget migrated to an unrelated 122px SVG in section E. Nothing in SKILL.md, run.md, verify.md or floor/buy.md asks the question that would have caught this, and it is upstream of every check we own.

2. Nothing on the page is lit, and the one drawn artefact carries a disclaimer. P's --kanalfyld is the right instinct (a 90deg three-stop gradient is a cylinder seen from the side) applied where it cannot be seen. There is no curvature overlay, no specular, no stated light direction, and the roll SVG is 30 hand-placed flat rects with a caption that defends its accuracy rather than adding a fact. The disclaimer is the diagnostic: a drawing detailed enough to be mistaken for a measurement and not physical enough to be read as an object is drawn at the wrong fidelity.

3. The signature has no dosage decision and no risk defence of the device. P's channel runs down every section from header to footer, so the mark is a page frame. P's §Risk describes the page's posture (leads with faults, red reserved for damage, no photography, yellowish ground) rather than defending the device against the failure mode it is nearest to. Q writes both: dosage once loud and once still, one named ornament deleted to protect it, and a device defence that states the parameters keeping an infinite ambient loop on the right side of motion-without-a-reason.

Worth recording that P beats Q on the things our package does enforce. P's field structure with A to F letters set inside the headings, its margin glossary notes, its five findings physically aligned to their marks on the channel, and its refusal to invent trade facts are all stronger and more its own than anything in Q's body. The judges' verdict is exactly right in both directions: our page is better, their one device is better, and the gap is entirely in how the device was specified before code.
found.notWorthTaking:
Five things, three of them praised.

1. The ten stop lists. Roughly 1.5 KB of hand-tuned magic numbers, ten lanes of about seven stops each over a 320px period, unparameterised and untunable. Anyone reusing them copies the rhythm and gets Q's roll, which is convergence in its purest form. Q's own plan says 240px over 8s while the code ships 320px over 10s, which is the proof that a stop table cannot be planned, only fiddled. Take the lane-and-period structure; never carry a stop table, a lane count or a duration into any file in this package.

2. The brass palette. #6B521A, #E0C066 at 38%, #C6A344 at 62%, #755A1C, and the messing pair #6E5210 / #B08F2E. These belong to brass in a piano workshop. Carrying the hexes is the 'bottle green plates' failure exactly. What transfers is the off-centre highlight position and the one-directional cast shadow, both stated without a colour.

3. The moving hero band as a general move, which is the thing most likely to be taken and should not be. Q's plan concedes in writing that an infinite ambient loop in a hero is normally motion without a reason, and defends it only because the transport IS the product. It also gets away with it because the band sits above the price and there is no basket; under floor/buy.md, nothing moves near money, and P's whole static stance follows correctly from that. The extractable clause is not the band, it is the defence: a device standing next to a known failure mode must state the parameters that keep it on the right side.

4. Everything below the band. Q's body is category furniture end to end: a label-left content-right spread repeated for six sections, a four-up numbered step row, a three-up stat row, one dark inverted section, a two-up people grid, a three-up footer facts row. That is the judges' 'one very good signature bolted to a very standard page', and it is precisely what P does not do. Nothing from Q's page structure should reach the package, and no proposal here should make a strong signature cheaper to buy a standard page with. Note that verify.md render question 6, cover the top third and ask whether the rest still says what this is, would fail Q honestly answered, so the check we already own is adequate and needs no change.

5. The reuse trick and the accessibility handling. .rulle--stille reusing the same markup with .spor:nth-child(n+7){display:none}, and role="img" with a Danish aria-label on the band, are both competent and neither is a technique. They are what a careful build does with a device it already has, and writing them down would be writing down carefulness.

techniques.name: An identifier is declared, worn, and said back
techniques.howItIsBuilt: T runs one address scheme through three separate surfaces and then makes the copy use it. The cover carries a real contents list (.contents ol, six …) that DECLARES 01–06. The sticky rail (.rail/.tab) repeats the same six as tabs. Each section WEARS its number in a boxed .sec-num beside the title. Then the prose CITES it: the cover CTA's sub-label reads "Afsnit 01", and section 02 closes with "se afsnit 01". The set inside section 02 gets sub-addresses DERIVED from the section's own number, 02.1 to 02.5, one per .fault article, so the five faults are catalogue parts rather than five cards. Nothing in this is decorative: every token is a retrieval address used by something else on the page.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: Our A–F letters appear exactly once each, inside their own h2 (.bogstav span). Nothing declares them (P has no contents, no nav, no in-page anchors beyond the skip link), nothing targets them (the sections carry aria-labelledby but no addressable id for the letter), and the prose never says a letter back. An identifier used once is a label; a label costs nothing and therefore forces nothing downstream. This is the actual cascade that made T a world: the contents panel made every section an addressable unit, addressable units forced numbers, a numbered section holding a set forced sub-addresses, five sub-addresses forced five distinguishable objects, five objects forced a shared drawing convention, and the convention then paid for the cover elevation's callouts. One decision at the top with no exit at any step. P's letters had an exit at every step.
techniques.sitesmithForm: SKILL.md §6 Structure, replacing the current paragraph: "**Structure.** A structural device has to encode something true, and then be used. Numbering, eyebrows, dividers and tabs each claim something: `01/02/03` claims order. Cut the ones that claim nothing. An identifier that survives is declared in one place, worn by the thing it names, and said back by the copy or a control that points with it. Used once, it is a label, and a label forces nothing downstream." Displaces SKILL.md §1's rhetorical closing sentence ("They will recognise that feeling again instantly, and \"it passed all the checks\" will not save you.", ~25 tokens), which is framing, not instruction. Net cost to the always-loaded surface is about zero. Enforcement in gate.mjs, which already parses the built HTML: detect schemes (tokens matching ^\d{2}$, ^\d{2}\.\d+$, ^[A-Z]$) repeating across three or more headings or sibling elements; per scheme count roles — declared (the token set appears in a nav or list of in-page links), worn (appears in or beside the heading of the section it names), cited (appears in body prose outside its own section or in a control's label). Refuse a scheme found at one role only, naming the tokens. A scheme whose tokens prefix-match a passing scheme (02.1 under 02) inherits its declaration. The check only fires on schemes already present, so a build with no identifiers is untouched and no build is pushed to grow a contents list.
techniques.risk: Agents may read it as "add a table of contents", which would converge. The conditional framing and the fire-only-when-present check are what hold that off; if the check ever refuses a page for having no scheme, the rule has inverted and must be pulled.

techniques.name: The signature names its dependents
techniques.howItIsBuilt: T's boldness is not one element, it is one logic with four dependents. Yolk (#e8b304) is the annotation ink: it marks damage in every fault drawing (stroke #e8b304 over black keylines), it draws the callout leaders and circled numbers on the cover elevation, it fills the contents panel, it fills the active tab under :target, and it fills the price and stock plates. The condensed axis works the same way: wdth 66–78 at wght 650–850 for anything structural, wdth 100 at wght 420–520 for anything read. Each element on the page answers to something the signature established.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P's Signature line names `.kanal` and the channel is genuinely a better idea than T's tab rail: it explains why the five faults belong together, which five cards could not. But it has exactly one dependent, the five red marks (.optælling li::after), and outside section B the channel is an empty aria-hidden div repeating a gradient in every section while nothing attaches to it. The margin notes, the panel, the folk list, the roll drawing and the footer would all survive unchanged if the channel were deleted. SKILL.md §6 as written asks for one signature and says "keep everything around it quiet", and a literal reading of that produces exactly P: one bold device surrounded by neutral ones. Quiet is not the same as unrelated.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Zero cost to any budgeted file. ledger.mjs's template() already writes per-heading format hints that parseDirection strips (line 96), which is where the `Built:` and `For:` line formats live. Add under Signature: "> format: Dependents: `<selector>` — <the token it takes from the signature>, one per line. An element that could be swapped without touching the signature is not one." gate.mjs already extracts the signature's selector (line 211) and looks it up in the DOM (line 1132); extend it to refuse when a Signature selector exists with no Dependents line, when a named dependent selector is absent from the DOM, and when the token named on a dependent line does not appear in the declarations of both that selector and the signature's. Retrieval and refusal only: the script never says which token or which element.

techniques.name: Drawings are a set before they are drawings
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Six inline SVGs, one convention. Every fault drawing uses ink keylines at stroke-width 2.4 with no fill for the part, and a second ink (yolk, stroke-width 3 to 3.4) reserved for the one thing asserted: the perished pocket, the split hose, the crack in the wind trunk. The cover elevation is the same convention at scale, stroke 3 and 2 for the instrument, yolk only for callout leaders and circled numbers. The caption .cut-cap is a real key: circled 1 and 2 whose tokens exist as <text> elements inside the drawing they caption. Every drawing carries a <title> describing what it shows, not what it is.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P ships one drawing, the perforated roll, and P's own direction.md is right that no photography exists and everything must be drawn. The five findings, which are the page's substance, get an h3 and a paragraph each. So the one place P had to invent a visual language, it drew a single object instead of a convention, and the five things a reader would use to recognise their own instrument have nothing to look at. buy.md already says a labelled placeholder is a finished answer where the photograph does not exist; T shows the rung above that, and it is the rung that turns "no photos" from a constraint into the page's material.

A drawing that points carries a key, and every entry in the key exists in the drawing. The convention is free." techniques.risk: The reported palette table will read as a score unless it is printed under a heading that states these are observations with no target value. Keep the refusal to the two objective cases (missing title, unresolvable key) or the script starts choosing inks.

techniques.name: :target is a real state on a page with no script
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Six lines of CSS and no JavaScript: `body:has(#s01:target) .tab[href="#s01"]{background:var(--yolk);color:var(--ink)}` for each of the six, plus `section:target .sec-num{background:var(--yolk);color:var(--ink);border-color:var(--yolk)}`. Both ends of the jump acknowledge it — the index that sent you and the section you arrived at — and `section{scroll-margin-top:calc(var(--rail) + 2px)}` keeps the arrival clear of the sticky rail. T's own head comment calls it "the one authored state", which is the correct claim: it is the only state on the page and it was chosen.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P authors no state at all. Its only in-page anchor is the skip link, so nothing on the page can change and there is nothing for the state roster to walk. verify.md demands that every interactive element owe six states and that a state existing only in the plan is a missing state, but it says nothing about the case a document-shaped static page actually has, which is navigation. This is the cheapest device in the whole source and the one that most changes how the page reads: it is why T behaves like a document with pages rather than a scroll.

(33 tokens). Pay for it by trimming three justifying clauses already in that file — "and each one prevents a named failure", "because something that looks pressable and does nothing is a bug", and "Fewer than four and it is a smoke test, not a journey." (about 38 tokens together, none of which carries a rule the surrounding sentences do not already state). Net about minus 5 tokens against a 1-token headroom. Enforcement in verify.mjs, which already renders: follow each in-page href="#id" and diff computed styles across the document before and after; refuse when a page carries three or more in-page anchors and no anchor produces any computed-style difference anywhere. Under three anchors the check does not fire, so it never mandates navigation that a direction did not choose.
techniques.risk: Low. The failure mode is cosmetic uniformity if every build lights a tab in the accent colour; the obligation is that the state exists and is visible at both ends, and how it shows stays free.

techniques.name: Structure inventory printed with the render
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Not a device in T, a measurement that separates T from P and that neither build's report currently carries. Counted from the two files: distinct full-width grounds (T alternates stock and flooded green across six bands plus two yolk plates; P has one paper ground plus a dark footer, separated by 1px hairlines); inline drawings (T six, P one); identifier schemes and the role count of each (T two schemes at three roles; P one scheme at one role); repeated key/value registers in tabular mono (T five — .spec, .rows, .contents-foot, .stock-plate, .addr; P two).

They are the arity of the world, and arity is the whole difference here. Printing them costs no budgeted prose and decides nothing: P's single ground is defensible and was chosen in its plan ("Et trykt ark har ét udseende"), and a build whose direction argues for one ground should print 1 and pass. What the line makes impossible is finishing a build without noticing that its one device was used once.

No obligation, no gate, no target values, and the heading must say so. Pure retrieval.
techniques.target: scripts/verify.mjs + the design record section of the report

techniques.name: The variable axis carries the register instead of a second family

It then assigns axis values per role rather than faces per role: headings wdth 78 wght 800 uppercase, wordmark wdth 66 wght 850, rail tab names wdth 66 wght 650, body wdth 100 wght 420, data values wdth 100 wght 520, price plate wdth 72 wght 850. But it means P's hierarchy is carried by family switching, while T's condensation is itself a hierarchy signal that scales continuously and costs one font request.
techniques.sitesmithForm: SKILL.md §6 Type, added to the two-roles sentence: "Two roles need not be two families: where the face has axes, name the width or optical value that belongs to each role, so condensation carries hierarchy instead of a second typeface." It has no script behind it, which by this repository's own rule makes it the weakest of the set.
techniques.risk: High, and specific. One step from this permission is condensed uppercase headings on every build, which is the round-8 house style this repository has already blocked once. It is also prose with no check behind it. Take it last or not at all.

techniques.name: The signature declares a measure, and something that is not decorative is built from it
techniques.howItIsBuilt: U hands the punch's own dimensions to the token layer and then spends them elsewhere. `--rail:116px` is the `punch-v` tile width to the pixel; `--slot-tall:26px` is the `punch-h` tile height to the pixel; `--slot-pitch:44px` is the tallest hole and `--slot-w:12px` is a hair over its width. `.num .slot{width:var(--slot-pitch);height:var(--slot-w);border-radius:var(--radius-full)}` then draws every section numeral as one of those holes rotated, and the cutaway's punched paper reuses the same `width="11" rx="5.5"` capsule. The numerals are not decoration borrowed from the rail; they are the rail's gauge doing a second, non-decorative job.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P has no shared gauge anywhere. `--rørW:18px` sets the pipe, `width="6"` sets the holes in the roll drawing, `height:9px` sets the red damage marks: three unrelated numbers for what is conceptually the same trade's perforation. So P's rail reads as a graphic placed next to the page and U's reads as the page being one object. This is what the judges recorded as section numerals drawn in the same rhythm and pitch, and it is the single cheapest cause of the craft gap.
techniques.sitesmithForm: SKILL.md section 6, Signature paragraph. Replace the sentence "A texture rendered in three lines of CSS beats an expensive effect that could belong to anyone." with: "Give it a measure. One dimension of it becomes a named token, and at least one element that is not decorative is built from that token: a numeral, a rule, a gap. The page then reads as one object rather than a page with a graphic on it." To stay inside the 3,100 ceiling this also displaces, from the Colour paragraph, "A saturated colour usually clears contrast against some of your values and not others. Measure before you set a paragraph in one." (about 32 est tokens) which is prose duplicating a check verify.mjs already performs and section 8 already numbers at 4.5:1. Verified against both builds: U passes on `--slot-w` (referenced by `.num .slot`, outside `.roll-rail`); P has no such token and fails.

techniques.name: At the container's own hinge the signature becomes a different thing, not a smaller one
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Two transposed tilesets in one `<defs>`, swapped by `display` at the breakpoint, while the grid swaps the box's axis and the border moves from `border-right` to `border-bottom`. `--container:1000px` is the only number: `min-width:1000px` opens the numeral hanging column, `max-width:999px` turns the rail into a band. No transform, no JS, no second asset.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P's only responsive move for its signature is `@media (max-width:640px){:root{--rende:30px;--rørX:7px;--rørW:12px}}`, which makes the pipe thinner. At 375 that pipe still eats 30px off every line's measure and gives nothing back. U's band costs 26px of page height once and stays legible. The judges called the rotation the single cleverest responsive move in the set; the generalisable part is not the rotation, it is that the signature was required to have a second form and to earn its space in that form.
techniques.sitesmithForm: verify.md, question 3 of the six. Replace "**Is the signature visible at 1440 and alive at 375?**" with "**Is the signature visible at 1440, and at 375 is it a different thing rather than a smaller one?**" To stay inside 4,600 this displaces "The scripts measure. techniques.risk: An aspect-ratio comparison misfires on signatures that are correct to keep the same shape at both widths, a repeated stamp, a monospaced rule, a colour field. The written-reason escape is what makes it survivable, and without that escape this becomes a script deciding a design. The prose half is near-certain; the check is the uncertain half.

techniques.name: A drawing standing in for a photograph states its correspondence and its status
techniques.howItIsBuilt:
The cutaway's five callouts are `circle r=14 fill=var(--ink)` with `text fill=var(--surface)`, numbered 1 to 5. The same five numerals appear as `01` on the five `
` beside it. The caption then says the correspondence in words and declares the drawing schematic: the numbers on the drawing are the numbers on the list, and the drawing shows the path from pedals to hammer, not a particular instrument. The 800-character `aria-label` walks the same path in the same order, so the non-visual reading is the drawing rather than a label about it.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P declares its roll drawing schematic and not a measured drawing, which is half of this, but it has no marked drawing at all: P's five faults are numbered against red marks on a CSS pipe, and the mechanism is carried entirely in one paragraph of prose. P's own direction.md records abolishing the plate block on purpose as an originality move. Defensible, and in a brief with zero photography it cost the page its strongest possible asset. buy.md already lists measured drawings as one of three ways to satisfy the imagery obligation and gives no instruction on how a drawing earns its place.
techniques.sitesmithForm: floor/buy.md, appended to the "Imagery says what a photograph cannot" obligation, in that file's existing form of obligation plus free axis: "A drawing that carries reference marks repeats those marks verbatim in the running text, and its caption states which kind of drawing it is, so a schematic cannot be read as a measurement. The mark vocabulary is free." Enforcement: gate.mjs, where an inline `<svg>` contains `<text>` nodes matching a bare numeral or single capital, each such string must also occur in the document text outside that svg, and the svg must carry a `<figcaption>` or non-empty `aria-label`. Retrieval and refusal only.
techniques.risk: Belongs equally in floor/operate.md and is scoped here only to keep the cost honest, so a tool surface with a marked diagram is not covered. The check false-positives on a drawing whose numerals are axis ticks or a scale bar; it should skip svgs inside a figure marked as a chart.

techniques.name: No literal colour and no per-shape stroke width inside an inline drawing
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Every fill and stroke in U's rail and cutaway is `var(--void)`, `var(--ink)`, `var(--line)` or `var(--surface)`. No shape carries a `stroke-width` attribute; `.plate svg g{stroke-width:var(--stroke)}` sets all of them from one 1.6px token. That is why U's drawings follow the `prefers-color-scheme:dark` block that redefines `--void` and `--ink`, and why the line weight of the whole cutaway is one number.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P's roll drawing hardcodes `fill="#E6D9BB" stroke="#8C6316"`, `stroke="#5A5648"`, `fill="#3A2318"`. Six literals that duplicate `--rullepapir`, `--messingstreg`, `--blyrør` and `--valnød`. Change any of those tokens and the drawing keeps the old paper. It is one reason P can only declare `color-scheme:light`. P also proves the same page can do better: `.fod{--messingstreg:var(--messinglys)}` re-declares a token at the inverted scope so the CSS pipe survives the dark band, exactly the move the SVG was denied.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Zero prose on any loaded surface, which is the strongest form available given the budgets and satisfies "prose is never the enforcement" completely. One gate.mjs check on the built artifact: refuse `render/drawing-carries-a-literal-colour` for any `fill=` or `stroke=` inside an inline ``: U's own favicon uses `fill='%23f2e9d8'` and would fail a careless implementation.
techniques.target: scripts/gate.mjs only; one supporting line optional in stacks/static.md, which has room under the 6,200 routine ceiling
techniques.risk: Costs nothing on the always-loaded surface and nothing to read, but it is a hard refusal on a pattern that is occasionally correct: a drawing quoting a real brand's exact colours, or a logo. Needs the same written-reason escape as the others. The data-URI exclusion is not optional; without it the check fails a build that is right.

techniques.name: A field that must run an unknown length is tiled in user space, not scaled
techniques.howItIsBuilt: The rail svg has no viewBox, so user units are CSS pixels, and its `<pattern patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">` tiles over a `<rect width="100%" height="100%">`. Whether the page is 2,000px or 12,000px long, the holes stay 11px wide. The alternative every model reaches for first, a viewBox fitted to the element or a background-image sized to cover, stretches the marks as the page grows and the distortion is invisible in a 1440 screenshot of the first fold.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P's roll is a fixed `viewBox="0 0 130 300"` with thirty hand-written rects at `max-width:122px`. It is a picture of a roll rather than a length of one, it cannot grow, and thirty literal rects is three times the source text for a third of the coverage. Nothing in v3 says which of the two an unbounded field should be.
techniques.sitesmithForm: stacks/static.md, after the "If CSS can do it, use CSS" paragraph: "A drawn field that has to run a length you do not know is a tiled pattern in user space, not a fitted drawing. Give the element no viewBox so its units are pixels, and let the tile repeat; a drawing scaled to fit changes the size of its own marks as the page grows, and a first-fold screenshot will not show it." Enforcement is only partial and should be stated as such: gate.mjs can refuse `preserveAspectRatio="none"` on an inline svg, which catches the crude version of this defect and not the subtle one.
techniques.risk: The weakest entry by this repository's own rule, because the check catches only the blatant case and the rest is prose. It also lives in a stack adapter, so a React or Astro run never reads it. Narrow applicability: it only matters once a page has an unbounded drawn field, and an unbounded drawn field is itself close to the convergent shape flagged below.

found.whatOursLacks:
Five things, in the order they cost craft.

1. **The rail is segmented, not one object.** P renders `<div class="kanal">` inside every `.felt`, eight separate absolutely-positioned pipes with `top:0;bottom:0` of their own section. It only looks continuous because the sections abut, and `.felt+.felt{border-top:1px solid}` draws a hairline straight across the pipe at every join, which is an accident nobody chose and which direction.md does not mention. Any future gap between sections breaks the pipe silently and no check would see it. U draws one element for the whole page and the grid stretches it.

2. **No shared gauge.** `--rørW:18px`, `width="6"`, `height:9px`: three numbers for one idea. U's `--rail:116px` and `--slot-tall:26px` are the two pattern tiles to the pixel, and `--slot-pitch`/`--slot-w` carry that gauge into the numerals and the cutaway.

3. **Shrinkage where U has transformation.** P's only signature-level responsive move is making the pipe thinner at 640px, which still costs 30px of measure at 375 and returns nothing.

4. **The drawing is outside the token system.** Six hardcoded hexes; consequently `color-scheme:light` and no dark mode at all.

5. **No mechanism drawing.** P explains a pneumatic action in one paragraph of prose. U drew it, and the judges called it the best drawing anyone made. On a brief whose direction.md states in its own Assets section that no photography exists, the drawing was the load-bearing asset and v3 argued itself out of making one, recording the choice as an originality move.

What P has that U does not, so the comparison is honest: the branch stubs. `.optælling li::before` and `::after` reach out of the content column with `left:calc(-1*(var(--rende)+var(--indryk)-var(--rørX)-var(--rørW)))` to draw a spur and lay a red damage mark across the pipe at the exact vertical position of each of the five faults. That is a real device, it ties list to drawing physically rather than by numeral, and U has no equivalent. It is also fragile: it depends on the list being a direct child of `.indhold` at exactly `--indryk` padding, and it silently misaligns at any other nesting depth. And `.fod{--messingstreg:var(--messinglys)}` re-declaring a token so a drawn element survives a colour inversion is better than anything U does with scope. Neither is proposed above, because both are ours already.
found.notWorthTaking:
**The punched roll itself, and every dressing of it.** Buff paper, one felt red, Fraunces over IBM Plex Sans, holes as a texture. U's own DIRECTION.md is blunt about it: a plumber cannot use a perforated roll, and neither can a piano tuner, only the workshop that cuts rolls. Carrying any of it forward is carrying an appearance.

**"A full-height decorated left rail."** This is the trap in the whole exercise and it must be said plainly. It is a strong, handsome shape, it is trivially transplantable, and it would make three unrelated briefs converge on their next run. This repository has failed that test four times, and the last failure was five shared moves across three builds that each passed individual review. If any of the above reaches the skill phrased as a shape rather than as an obligation, it becomes the fifth. Everything proposed above is phrased as "the signature owes a measure" and "the signature owes a second form", never as "the signature is a rail", and that phrasing is the whole of the safety.

**The hanging-numeral margin.** `.col{padding-left:calc(...)}` cancelled by `section{margin-left:calc(...*-1)}`, one expression governing both sides of the gap, is good CSS and I am deliberately not proposing it. It is plumbing, not a design decision, and a layout recipe in an always-loaded surface is how a skill starts producing identical pages. Numerals hanging in a left margin would be recognisable across three briefs within a week.

**`section:target` recolouring the numeral and its slot.** Free, no JS, genuinely nice. Also a house tic waiting to happen: every anchor-navigated page picking up the same target treatment is the same convergence at smaller scale, and verify.md's state roster already demands states without prescribing which element carries them.

**The five-layer `<g>` stacking order of the cutaway** as a drawing method. It is correct for a cross-section of a machine and it is not general. A map, a specimen, a chart and a worn surface each want a different layering, and writing this one down would mean the next three drawings are cross-sections. What generalises from that drawing is only the two obligations in technique 3 and the hygiene in technique 4.

**`signature-min-share: 6`** from U's axis record. v2.3 required the signature to occupy a minimum share of the render. It is tempting because it is measurable, and it should stay dropped: it rewards making the signature bigger, which is the one direction that needs no encouragement, and a share threshold is a script deciding a design.
