docs/rebuild/s15/builds/S/index.html — Klinke & Datter, arm S. Read in full (672 lines) against our arm P (728 lines) and P's .sitesmith/direction.md.

THE PATTERN, not the sentences. S's prose is four sentence shapes in rotation, governed by one law.

The law: every sentence's grammatical subject is either the reader or the business. Never a nominalisation, never a passive. S writes "Vi kommer ud og vurderer"; we write "Vurderingen foregår hjemme hos dig og tager en halv dag." Same fact, but ours has an abstract noun as its actor, so nobody is doing anything and nobody can be held to it.

Shape 1, THE REFUSAL. A main clause with "ikke" in it, placed BEFORE the offer it justifies, never apologised for, never softened by an adverb. Seven on the page: "Det kan vi ikke svare på i telefonen." / "vi tager ikke andet ind" / "Det tager vi ikke" / "Vi giver ikke et tal før." / "Der er ikke andre" / "Første skridt er en samtale, ikke en formular." The first body sentence on the page denies the question the H1 just asked, and that denial is the entire reason the 1.850 kr. visit exists. The refusal is the product description.

Shape 2, THE PROCEDURE. One sentence, coordinated physical verbs, each with a place or a duration attached: "Vi kommer hjem til dig, bruger en halv dag på instrumentet og skriver ned, hvad vi finder." No verb in it could be performed by software.

Shape 3, THE RETENTION. Second person, and it names the failure branch out loud: "Du får rapporten, uanset om arbejdet bliver til noget eller ej." / "Bagefter ved du, hvad du står med [...] også hvis svaret er nej."

Shape 4, THE FLAT CONSEQUENCE. Five words or fewer, no subordination, no qualifier, carrying the unwelcome fact: "Der er som regel ventetid." / "Vi giver ikke et tal før." / "Der er ikke andre."

And the headings obey the same law. Every S section heading is a predication that could be false, so it carries information: "Vi arbejder kun med pneumatik" / "Fem fejl, vi nævner ved navn" / "Fire skridt, og du kender først prisen på restaureringen til sidst" / "To personer. Der er ikke andre" / "Ring, og fortæl hvad du har stående". The fourth of those puts the objection in the heading where the category puts the benefit.

The judges are right that the bones are borrowed. The writing is not on the bones. It survives being stripped to plain text, which is the test SKILL.md section 7 already names and which our arm fails.

techniques.name: The limit gets its own main clause
techniques.howItIsBuilt: S never subordinates an unwelcome fact. "Vi giver ikke et tal før." is five words, sentence-final, after a 24-word sentence explaining the four-to-nine-month restoration. "Fire instrumenter ad gangen. Der er som regel ventetid." splits capacity and its consequence into two sentences rather than joining them with a causal conjunction. The refusal always precedes the offer it justifies rather than following it as a caveat: the page's first body sentence is "Det kan vi ikke svare på i telefonen", and only then does the paid visit appear. No hedging adverbs anywhere: no "desværre", no "typisk", no "normalt" attached to a refusal.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: Our arm has the same limits and buries every one of them. P writes "Hvilke af dem der er tale om hos dig, kan vi først sige, når vi har stået ved instrumentet" — 17 words, fronted object clause, the limit arriving in a subordinate clause at the end. S's equivalent is "Vi giver ikke et tal før." P writes "Vi giver en pris, når vurderingen er lavet, og ikke før", which appends the refusal to a promise; S makes it the whole sentence. A limit in a subordinate clause reads as a hedge someone hopes you skim. In a main clause it reads as a person who knows the job and is not going to pretend otherwise. That is the single largest measurable delta between the two texts.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Replaces the interface-microcopy tail of SKILL.md section 7. New text: "**Put the limit in its own sentence.** What you will not do, what you cannot say yet, what is not included: each is a main clause with a subject and a verb, never a subordinate clause hung off a promise. The sentence carrying the unwelcome fact is the shortest in its paragraph and takes no qualifier." DISPLACES two things, both moved verbatim into floor/operate.md where controls and states actually live: (a) "Active voice by default: a control says what happens when it is used and keeps the same word all the way through, so a button that says Publish produces a message that says Published." (45 est tokens); (b) "Errors say what happened and what to do about it, in the interface's voice, and never apologise. An empty state is an invitation, not an apology." (36 est tokens). 81 freed against 75 added, so SKILL.md lands at roughly 3,089 of 3,100. The displacement is a consolidation, not arithmetic: the removed clause is about control labels in an operate surface, and the new one subsumes its active-voice requirement for the sentences that carry weight.
techniques.target: skills/sitesmith-v3/SKILL.md section 7 (with the displaced text landing in skills/sitesmith-v3/floor/operate.md)
techniques.risk: Nothing in the build output checks this, and the rules say prose is never the enforcement. It is honest to say so: this one is carried by technique 5's planning obligation, which forces the refusals to be written down per subject in the direction record before code, where ledger.mjs refuses a blank. Convergence risk is low because every subject's limits are different (a bakery's "vi bager ikke glutenfrit" and a ferry's "vi sejler ikke om vinteren" produce no shared page), but the risk is not zero: a rhythm of short flat sentences could become the next house style. Mitigated by the rule constraining only the sentences that carry limits, not the whole page.

techniques.name: An absent figure is answered where the figure would be
techniques.howItIsBuilt: S cannot price the restoration, and instead of going quiet it puts the absence in the section heading: "Fire skridt, og du kender først prisen på restaureringen til sidst." The heading tells you the count and the disappointment in one line. The step that would carry the price instead carries "Først derefter et tilbud" and "En fuld pneumatisk restaurering tager fire til ni måneder, og den bliver prissat efter vurderingen. Vi giver ikke et tal før." So the position where a price belongs holds three things: what determines the figure, when it arrives, and a flat statement that no earlier number exists.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P handles the same gap inside section D as a two-sentence aside: "Vi giver en pris, når vurderingen er lavet, og ikke før." It is true and it is placed where the reader is no longer asking. S answers the question at the moment it is asked, in the heading, before the reader has to go looking and conclude the number is being withheld. floor/buy.md currently has nine obligations, all of which assume a price exists ("The price is found, not hunted"). It has nothing for the quote-based trade, which is most of the small-business surfaces this skill will be pointed at.
techniques.sitesmithForm: New obligation in floor/buy.md, in that file's own idiom: heading, one paragraph naming the free axis, then "Three ways:". Proposed: "### An absent figure is answered where the figure would be — Where a price cannot be given until work is done, the page says so in the position a price would occupy, names what decides it, and names when the buyer gets it. A range invented to fill the space is a claim. Silence in that position reads as a figure being withheld. The wording is free. Three ways: the row exists and its value is the condition rather than a number; the section that would carry the price says the condition in its heading; the step list names the step at which the figure arrives."
techniques.risk: floor/buy.md is only opened on buy and redesign scenarios, so this never touches the always-loaded budget. The routine ceiling is 6,200 across run.md + floor + stacks; buy.md is currently around 850 est tokens, so 136 is affordable. Convergence risk is low because the file's three-ways form is built to prevent a single answer. Real risk: the "invented range is a claim" clause overlaps SKILL.md's existing claim rule, so it is partly redundant — I kept it because the failure it names (filling an empty price field with a plausible band) is exactly the one a model commits under layout pressure.

techniques.name: Section headings are predications, not labels
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Every h2 on S is a clause with a subject and a finite verb, and each could be false: "Vi arbejder kun med pneumatik", "Fem fejl, vi nævner ved navn", "Vi skærer nye ruller efter originale masters", "To personer. Der er ikke andre", "Ring, og fortæl hvad du har stående". The nav labels obey it too: "Det vi typisk finder" and "Sådan starter du" rather than "Typiske fejl" and "Proces". A reader who scans only the headings has been told what the business does, refuses, and charges.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: Four of our six section headings are bare nouns with a definite article: "Vurderingen", "Restaureringen", "Rullerne", "Værkstedet". A topic label cannot be false, so it carries no information and any competitor in the trade could use the identical six. Our A-to-F letters are a real structural idea and the headings they sit in are empty. This is also the failure verify.md's render question 5 is already reaching for ("Read the six largest words in order") without catching, because our largest words are the H1 and the amount, which are both fine.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Replace render-inspection question 5 in verify.md with: "**Read the section headings in order, alone. Does each make a claim that could be wrong?** A heading that only names a topic says nothing a competitor could not also say." DISPLACES the current question 5 (34 est tokens) plus two trims in the same file to cover the 8-token overrun: delete "There is always one." from question 2, and cut "the way the client will," from the paragraph above the list. That frees roughly 11 against 8 needed, landing verify.md at about 4,596 of 4,600.
techniques.risk: Moderate convergence risk, and it must stay a judgement question rather than a script. A verb-detector over h2 text is cheap to write and would be a script deciding a design, which the rules forbid; it is also unreliable in Danish, where a heading like "Fem fejl, vi nævner ved navn" and a label like "Fem fejl" differ by a relative clause a regex cannot see. The residual risk is that every page starts reading like a manifesto of first-person-plural claims. Mitigation is that verify.md's questions are answered one line each and then the agent fixes what it found, with a two-pass cap already in force.

techniques.name: Name what the first purchase leaves behind when the deal stops
techniques.howItIsBuilt: S states the worst branch twice in different words and once in the price block itself. The price list's third row is "Du får rapporten, uanset om arbejdet bliver til noget eller ej" — inside the panel, level with the figure, not further down as reassurance. The hero lead closes on "Bagefter ved du, hvad du står med [...] også hvis svaret er nej." Step 3 repeats it as "Den er din, uanset om der bliver en restaurering ud af det eller ej." The reader is told three times, in three registers, what 1.850 kr. buys them if the answer is no.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: We have the move and we blunt it. P uses the identical phrase "uanset om arbejdet går videre" twice, in the optakt and in section C, and once more in the footer. Same wording each time, and the wording never names the bad outcome: "går videre" is a neutral abstraction where S says "hvis svaret er nej". Naming the failure branch in the words the reader is privately using is what makes the concession land. floor/buy.md's "The whole commitment is legible before it is made" covers what is paid, waited for and returned; it does not cover what a paid diagnostic leaves behind when it recommends against the work, which is the shape of every survey, inspection, audit and consultation surface.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Second new obligation in floor/buy.md: "### The first step is worth having on its own — Where the purchase in front of the buyer is a step toward a larger one, the page says what this step leaves them holding if nothing follows, in the same place the figure is. Naming the branch in the buyer's own words, not in a neutral one. What it is called is free. Three ways: the deliverable is a row in the panel that carries the price; one sentence naming what the buyer keeps when the answer is no; a specimen of the deliverable shown at the size it arrives."
techniques.risk: Lower priority than the absent-figure obligation if only one can land, because it applies to a narrower class of surface (staged purchases) and because our arm already does a weak version, so the gain is a sharpening rather than a new capability. Convergence risk: every buy page acquiring a consolation sentence. The three-ways form limits it, and the obligation is conditional on the purchase actually being a first step, so most buy surfaces skip it.

techniques.name: The direction record plans the refusals before any code
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Not in the source. This is the enforcement the source's writing implies, built in the idiom ledger.mjs already uses. S's page reads as though someone listed what the workshop will not do before writing anything else: the refusals are load-bearing in the hero, in two section headings and in the contact block, which is not where a writer arrives by editing.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: Techniques 1, 2 and 4 are prose, and this repository's own gate.mjs comment says why prose fails: "an instruction every build reads becomes the next thing they all agree on. A check does not." ledger.mjs's REQUIRED array plus directionProblems already refuses a blank heading and already runs shape checks per section (the named() check requires "name: what it is for" lines under Colour and Type; the runner-up block requires a For: line and two sentences). Adding one heading makes the refusals a planning artefact per subject rather than a style every subject inherits, which is the only version of this that does not make three briefs converge.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Add 'Refusals' to REQUIRED in skills/sitesmith-v3/scripts/ledger.mjs, positioned after 'Argument order'. The template is generated from REQUIRED (template() loops it), so the cost is one array entry and no second literal to keep in sync. Add a shape check in directionProblems alongside the existing named() checks: the body must carry at least two lines, since one refusal is a caveat and two is a position. Message in the file's existing voice: "the \"Refusals\" section names fewer than two things this page will not claim, will not do, or cannot answer yet, written in this subject's own terms". Zero cost to SKILL.md, run.md and verify.md: run.md step 3 already says the script owns the heading list so that file does not repeat it, so nothing in a budgeted prose surface changes.
techniques.risk: Cost is real but lands in code, not in a budgeted prose file. Two risks. First, an agent can satisfy a two-line minimum with two restatements of the same refusal; the existing jaccard similarity check used on the runner-up block is the obvious defence and I have not sized that work. Second, every existing direction record in the repo, including docs/rebuild/s15/builds/P/.sitesmith/direction.md, becomes non-conforming the moment the heading is added, so this needs a migration decision before it lands. Do not ship it silently.

techniques.name: The commit control keeps one wording; the quiet links carry the reader's question
techniques.howItIsBuilt: S has three phone links and gives them three labels. The two filled commit controls both read "Ring 66 12 47 09", identical. The quiet ones read "Se hvordan en vurdering foregår" and "Spørg til titlerne på 66 12 47 09" — each naming the sentence the reader would actually say at that point on the page, with the number carried inside the label so the action is never in doubt. The nav follows the same instinct: "Sådan starter du" is written from the reader's side, "Det vi typisk finder" from the workshop's.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: P uses "Ring 66 12 47 09" three times, identically, including on the roll section where the reader's actual question is which titles are in stock. Our page never once puts the reader's own words in a control. The distinction matters and is easy to get wrong in the other direction: SKILL.md section 7 currently requires a control to keep the same word all the way through, which is right for a commit control and wrong for a contextual quiet link. Separating the two is the point.
techniques.sitesmithForm: One added free-axis line under the existing "One control commits, and it is always in reach" obligation in floor/buy.md: "The committing control keeps one wording wherever it appears. A quiet link beside it may instead name the question the buyer has at that point, so long as the action is unambiguous from the label." No new heading, no new three-ways block.
techniques.target: skills/sitesmith-v3/floor/buy.md, under the existing commit-control obligation
techniques.risk: Smallest gain of the six and the most easily misread as licence to vary the commit control's label, which is the failure the existing obligation exists to prevent. Only worth landing if the sentence keeps "keeps one wording" first and the permission second. Skip it if buy.md is tight after techniques 2 and 4.

found.whatOursLacks:
Five concrete deltas, all in the text, none in the layout.

1. NOMINALISATIONS AS SUBJECTS. Ours: "Vurderingen foregår hjemme hos dig og tager en halv dag." Theirs: "Vi kommer ud og vurderer." Ours has an abstract noun doing the acting in the one sentence that describes the service the page is selling. Every process sentence on S has du or vi as its subject.

2. LIMITS IN SUBORDINATE CLAUSES. Ours: "Hvilke af dem der er tale om hos dig, kan vi først sige, når vi har stået ved instrumentet" (17 words, fronted object clause, limit arrives last). Theirs: "Vi giver ikke et tal før." Ours: "Vi giver en pris, når vurderingen er lavet, og ikke før" — the refusal appended to a promise. Theirs makes it the sentence.

3. TOPIC LABELS FOR HEADINGS. Ours: "Vurderingen", "Restaureringen", "Rullerne", "Værkstedet" — four of six headings are bare nouns that cannot be false. Theirs: "Vi arbejder kun med pneumatik", "Fem fejl, vi nævner ved navn", "Fire skridt, og du kender først prisen på restaureringen til sidst", "To personer. Der er ikke andre". Their heading carries the objection where ours carries a filing category.

4. THE FAILURE BRANCH NAMED IN NEUTRAL WORDS. Ours says "uanset om arbejdet går videre" three times, identical wording, abstract. Theirs says "uanset om arbejdet bliver til noget eller ej", "Den er din, uanset om der bliver en restaurering ud af det eller ej", and "også hvis svaret er nej" — three registers, and the third one names the outcome the reader is privately dreading.

5. THREE IDENTICAL CONTROL LABELS. Ours ships "Ring 66 12 47 09" three times, including on the music-roll section where the reader's question is which titles exist. Theirs varies the quiet links to the reader's own question and keeps the commit control fixed.

What ours does better, so this is not one-directional: our fault list explains the mechanism ("Bælgen suger luften ud, og hullerne i rullen lukker luft ind gennem trakterstangen") and our fault headings are predications ("Lommelæderet er smuldret") where theirs are noun phrases ("Mørnet pungelæder"). Our margin notes define one trade term per section at the point of use. None of that was enough, because the sentences carrying the transaction were the weak ones.
found.notWorthTaking:
Six things, three of them praised by the judges.

THE OPENING REFUSAL AS A DEVICE. "Det kan vi ikke svare på i telefonen" is the best sentence on the page and the most dangerous to generalise. It works because the business genuinely cannot diagnose remotely and sells the diagnosis; the refusal IS the product. A page that opens by refusing where the business could have answered reads as obstruction, and a model told to "open with a refusal" will manufacture one. What transfers is the grammar of a limit, not the position of this limit. If a subject has no true limit at the top, there is no sentence to write there.

"FØRSTE SKRIDT ER EN SAMTALE, IKKE EN FORMULAR." The judges credited this with earning the phone-only contact, and they are right, but the reason it is earned is that the brief supplied no facts about response times or what a form would collect, so a form would have required inventing both. That is a constraint, not a principle. Encoded as a rule it becomes "prefer phone", which is wrong for most surfaces and would be a liability the moment three briefs met it. The generalisable residue is thin and I have deliberately not proposed it: when a page omits a control the category always has, saying the omission in words is better than leaving a hole. That is one sentence of guidance and it is not worth a budget line.

THE EM DASHES. S uses three, and its single best line depends on one for its beat: "Bagefter ved du, hvad du står med — også hvis svaret er nej." Our SKILL.md bans them absolutely and gate.mjs refuses them in build output at copy/em-dash, so any sentence lifted verbatim from this source fails our own gate. This is not a conflict to resolve; the full-stop version is better under our own rule, because it turns the concession into its own sentence, which is exactly technique 1. Do not import the punctuation and do not weaken the ban to accommodate the source.

THE DANISH-PLUS-ENGLISH GLOSS. "Mørnet pungelæder / Pouch leather" across all five faults reads as expertise here because pneumatic-piano literature is English-dominant and the reader has probably already searched in English. In a trade with no foreign literature the same habit produces a page of pointless parentheses. Our own arm already handles this better by glossing inline and once ("På engelsk tracker bar"), which is the version that survives a change of trade. Nothing to take.

THE 01/02/03 STEPS. The judges called them out and they were right: S renders them with counter(trin, decimal-leading-zero). The four steps do have a true order, so numbering is defensible, but the leading zero is decoration and the eyebrow above each section repeats the nav label seven times. None of that is writing and none of it should be carried.

THE FIVE FAULT NAMES AS NOUN PHRASES. S's fault list is noun phrases with no verbs, which contradicts the heading rule I am extracting from the same page. That is not an inconsistency to reconcile, it is a boundary: a catalogue of named objects is a list, and lists take noun phrases. The predication rule belongs to section headings, which make an argument. If technique 3 lands in verify.md it must say "section headings", not "headings", or it will start rewriting inventories into sentences.

techniques.name: The segment timeline: scroll is a flat ordered list of weighted stages, not a set of triggers
techniques.howItIsBuilt: scrub-engine.js builds one flat array before anything renders (lines 86-102): SECTIONS are interleaved with CONNECTORS into SEGMENTS, each carrying a scroll weight `w` in viewport-heights (`s.scroll || DIVE_W`). layout() (182-191) accumulates that into absolute pixel bands — `s.start = off*vh; off += s.w; s.end = off*vh` — and sets the whole document height to `totalW*vh + vh`. read() (222-242) then asks one question per segment: `clamp((y - s.start)/(s.end - s.start), 0, 1)`. Nothing observes anything. There is no IntersectionObserver, no per-element trigger, no ordering logic; the order IS the array and the position IS arithmetic. Two details carry over intact and cost nothing: a segment may be null (line 96, a connector that failed to generate) and the chain still completes by crossfading its neighbours directly; and the seam band is `smooth(1 - outside/fade)` over a fixed vh crossfade, so segments overlap by a declared distance rather than by whatever the elements happen to do. Strip the video and the model is unchanged: a segment is a named span of scroll that yields one number.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: SiteSmith has no scene model at all. SKILL.md section 6 says a moving page gets "one deliberate moment", and nothing in run.md, verify.md or the floors says how a moment is constructed — while ledger.mjs REQUIRED forces the builder to fill a "Density, motion and boldness" heading. So the package demands a motion decision and supplies no vocabulary for one. The fallback that gets built is N independent scroll-reveal triggers, which is exactly what section 6 calls machine made ("scattered hover effects read as machine made because nobody chose them") with no alternative offered. The timeline is the alternative, and it is a technique rather than a look because what varies between builds is the segment list itself, which comes from section 3's nouns. A bindery gets fold, sew, trim, press. A shipping company gets berth, crane, manifest. Neither is derivable from the other and neither is derivable from the page outline.
techniques.sitesmithForm: An obligation in a new off-surface file `moment.md`, written in floor/buy.md's exact shape: the obligation, the sentence naming what it leaves free, then "Three ways" that look nothing alike. Heading: "The moment is a timeline of the subject's own stages, not of the page's sections." Free axis: count and content. The file ends with a floor-style audit line, and this is the one that does the anti-convergence work: hand the segment list to a business in another trade, and if the same list still describes its process then the segments are the page's outline in costume and there is no moment. `moment.md` is opened only when the direction record's motion field says the page moves, and put down again.
techniques.target: New file skills/sitesmith-v3/moment.md. Reached by a token-neutral swap inside SKILL.md section 6 Signature: the existing sentence "If the page moves, that is one deliberate moment and it comes from the same nouns; scattered hover effects read as machine made because nobody chose them." (155 chars) becomes "If the page moves, that is one deliberate moment and it is a timeline: open `moment.md`. Scattered hover effects read as machine made because nobody chose them." (157 chars). Net cost to the always surface at 3,095 of 3,100: zero. run.md and verify.md are not touched at all.
techniques.risk: Highest-risk item in this set, and it is the repository's known failure mode. The medium's first answer to "scroll timeline" is pinned full-viewport sections that crossfade, and three unrelated briefs would converge on it inside a week. Two things contain it and both must ship or the technique should not: the obligation says the segments are the subject's stages and explicitly refuses the hero/features/pricing list, and the audit line tests the segment list by handing it to another trade. A second risk is scope: a timeline invites a whole-page takeover, where section 6's rule is one moment with everything around it quiet. The file must say the timeline governs one moment, not the document.

techniques.name: A segment is a pure function of one number, so the page is correct at any entry point
techniques.howItIsBuilt: This is Remotion's composition model, held as an idea only: a scene is f(one number) and holds no animation state, which is why a Remotion frame can be rendered in any order on any machine. scroll-world arrives at the same place from the other direction and says it out loud in SKILL.md step 4: "scroll is a scrubber: visitors can scroll up, so every move also plays in reverse." The engine never stores progress — read() recomputes every segment's number from scrollY on every frame (222-242), and raf() (273-289) only lerps toward that target. No element is ever marked as having been seen. Ported off video: the segment element gets one custom property set from the same clamp, and CSS does the rest. `el.style.setProperty('--t', local)`, and the stylesheet reads `--t` for width, `stroke-dashoffset`, `object-position`, `translate`, whatever the moment actually is. Forbidden by construction: a class added on entry and never removed, and any value that depends on which direction the reader arrived from.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: The default scroll-reveal is one-shot and stateful: `entry.isIntersecting -> classList.add('is-in'); observer.unobserve()`. That page is a different page depending on how you got there. Land on it from a deep link, refresh halfway down, hit back, or scroll upward, and the state differs from the scrolled-through state. SiteSmith has no rule against this and no check for it; verify.mjs measures the reduced-motion pass and horizontal overflow, and the state roster in verify.md walks controls, not scroll state. "Pure function of the number" removes the whole defect class rather than fixing instances of it, which is the standing preference for robust systems over one-off fixes, and it is what makes the timeline in technique one composable at all: segments can be reordered, added or dropped because none of them remembers anything.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Second obligation in `moment.md`, same shape. Heading: "One number per segment, and every moving thing is a function of it." Body names the clamp, says set it once as a custom property and let CSS read it, and refuses the class that is added and never removed and the value that depends on which way the reader came. Free axis: the property it drives. Three ways, each a different physical claim: `--t` scales one rule's width so a measure is being taken; `--t` drives `stroke-dashoffset` so a line is being drawn; `--t` steps `object-position` so an object turns.
techniques.target: skills/sitesmith-v3/moment.md, second section. No other file changes.
techniques.risk: Low as a rule, moderate as an invitation. "One variable drives everything" reads to a model as permission to build a CSS-custom-property showcase, which is a look and belongs to one build. The three ways are chosen so that each drives a different kind of thing rather than three flavours of transform. Licence note: this obligation is informed by Remotion and copies nothing from it — remotion-skills carries no licence, so no text, structure or file from it may be reused, and none is. The clamp and the scrubber framing come from scroll-world, which is MIT and needs a line in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md if any code is lifted verbatim.

techniques.name: The dwell curve: weight the segment that carries the argument, and pin the remap's endpoints
techniques.howItIsBuilt: scrub-engine.js line 178: `lingerEase(x, L) = (1-L)*x + L*(4*(x-0.5)^3 + 0.5)`, applied in read() as `s.target = s.linger ? lingerEase(local, s.linger) : local`. The cubic term has zero slope at the midpoint and slope 3 at the edges, so blended at strength L the segment runs at (1-L) speed through its middle and (1+2L) at its ends. The engine's own comment states the property that matters more than the formula: f(0)=0 and f(1)=1 always, so seam frames are untouched. The header caps L at 0.6 and calls 1 a full pause. It pairs with the second knob, per-segment `scroll` weight (line 90, `w: s.scroll || DIVE_W`), which buys a scene more scroll distance outright. SKILL.md step 4 states the intent plainly: the camera settles mid-scene exactly while the copy peaks, then picks up speed toward the seam. That is the whole idea, and it needs no video: scroll distance is not time, and you get to choose where the reader is standing when the important frame lands.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: This is the failure nobody in the package can currently name. A scroll-driven page whose segments are evenly weighted flashes its one important state past between two wheel ticks, and the reader has to hold the page still to read the copy that goes with it. SiteSmith has no pacing vocabulary at all, so the built answer is uniform section heights and a linear map. The two knobs are content-derived rather than aesthetic: which segment carries the argument is a section 4 question, already answered in the direction record. And the endpoint-pinning rule is the genuinely portable part — it is what lets a segment be reweighted without retuning the ones beside it, which is the difference between a timeline you can edit and a set of numbers nobody dares touch.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Third obligation in `moment.md`. Heading: "The important frame lands where the reader is standing." Body: scroll distance is not time; give the segment that carries the argument more weight than its neighbours, and remap its number so the middle is slow and the edges quick; any remap must satisfy f(0)=0, f(1)=1 and never decrease. Free axis: the curve. Three ways, deliberately including the option of no curve at all: the blended cubic with L at 0.6 or below; two segments where one would do, the second holding still; a weight of three viewport-heights and no remap.
techniques.target: skills/sitesmith-v3/moment.md, third section. The endpoint and monotonicity rule is also the cheapest thing in this whole proposal to enforce in code: sample any declared remap across 0..1 in verify.mjs and refuse f(0)!=0, f(1)!=1, or any decrease. That is a script verifying and refusing, never deciding a design.
techniques.risk: Low on convergence, since the free axis is a number and three unrelated briefs weighting three different segments produce three different reading experiences from identical code. The real risk is over-application: dwell on every segment reads as a page wading through mud, and it is the kind of thing that feels like craft while it is being added. The L cap and "give it to the segment that carries the argument" are the containment, and one of the three ways being "no remap at all" is deliberate.

techniques.name: Finished with no scroll and no script, and provably stateless
techniques.howItIsBuilt: Two mechanisms from scroll-world, generalised. First, loadClip() line 201 returns immediately under `reduce` — the clips are never fetched, the stills stay up and cross-dissolve, and read() line 238 keeps driving the still's transform. Reduced motion removes the work, not just the visible animation, which is already SiteSmith's section 8 wording and here has a concrete shape: the segments still exist as document order, and each one reads at its finished state. Second, the optional-segment rule at line 96: if connectors[i] is falsy the chain crossfades directly and the page still completes, so a piece that could not be produced does not take the sequence down with it. On a page with no video the equivalents are exact: the custom property defaults to 1 in the stylesheet, so JavaScript off means every segment is at its end state; and removing any segment leaves a page that still reads. The verification is the part the package can actually enforce, and it falls out of technique two: navigate directly to a segment's hash, screenshot, then scroll to the same segment from the top and screenshot again. A difference is state, and state is the defect. Add a reduced-motion completeness check to the same pass: any element carrying text that computes to near-zero opacity or sits clipped out of view in the reduced render is content waiting for a trigger that will never fire.
techniques.whyItBeatsOurs: verify.mjs already runs a reduced-motion pass (line 510) and already fails on animations still running and on transitions past the threshold. What it cannot currently see is the opposite defect, which is the common one: a scroll-reveal page under reduced motion where the JavaScript is correctly disabled and the content therefore stays at opacity 0 forever. The page passes every motion check by being blank. Nothing in the package catches that today, and no amount of prose would — this is precisely the case where prose is not the enforcement. The deep-link parity check is the other half and has no equivalent anywhere in the repo.
techniques.sitesmithForm: Fourth obligation in `moment.md`. Heading: "It is finished with no scroll and no script." Body states that under prefers-reduced-motion and with JavaScript off every segment reads at its finished state and the page says everything it says, that motion is the second reading and never the only one, and names verify.mjs as the thing that checks it. Free axis: how it degrades. Three ways: the custom property defaults to 1 in the stylesheet; the segments are ordinary sections and the timeline only pins them; the script never runs and nothing was ever hidden.
techniques.target: Prose in skills/sitesmith-v3/moment.md, fourth section. The checks themselves go into skills/sitesmith-v3/scripts/verify.mjs as code, which costs no token budget and needs no new text in verify.md — its Release commands block already names verify.mjs as the thing that runs the render matrix and floor measures, so the new measures arrive under an existing sentence. That is what keeps verify.md at 4,599 of 4,600 untouched.
techniques.risk: Low on design convergence, since it constrains degradation rather than appearance. The implementation risk is false failures: the deep-link and scrolled screenshots will differ innocently on lazy images, scroll-position-dependent sticky chrome and any legitimately deferred load, so the comparison needs a tolerance and should compare the segment's own region rather than the full viewport. Shipped too strict, it becomes a check people learn to ignore, which is worse than no check. Worth prototyping the tolerance against the existing benchmark builds before it fails a build.

found.source: scroll-world (MIT) — skills/scroll-world/SKILL.md and references/scrub-engine.js; and remotion-skills (NO LICENCE) — skills/remotion-create/SKILL.md and video-layout.md. Everything proposed from Remotion is idea only; no text, structure or file from it is reused. All copied mechanism and any lifted code comes from scroll-world and needs a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md line.
found.whatOursLacks: There is no scene model anywhere in sitesmith-v3. SKILL.md section 6 gives motion one clause ("If the page moves, that is one deliberate moment and it comes from the same nouns"), run.md gives it nothing, the two floors give it nothing, and verify.md's state roster walks controls rather than scroll state. Meanwhile scripts/ledger.mjs REQUIRED forces the builder to fill a heading called "Density, motion and boldness" before any code — so the package compels a motion decision and supplies no vocabulary to make one with. The predictable result is the medium's default: N one-shot IntersectionObserver fade-ups, which is the machine-made scattering section 6 names, offered no alternative and caught by no check. Three specific gaps: no way to say what a moving page is made of (a flat ordered list of weighted segments taken from the subject's own stages); no way to say where in the reader's scroll the important state lands (per-segment weight plus an endpoint-pinned dwell remap); and no test that a scroll-driven page is the same page at a deep link as it is after scrolling, which is the defect that stateful reveals produce every time. verify.mjs's reduced-motion pass currently catches motion that survives the preference but cannot catch its inverse, content that stays at opacity 0 forever because the trigger was correctly disabled.
found.notWorthTaking: Almost all of scroll-world, including the parts that are genuinely excellent. The seam law — connector endpoints must be the neighbouring clips' actual rendered frames, never the source still — is the deepest idea in the source and it does not transfer at all, because the seam problem is manufactured by the video pipeline: two renders of the same subject differ, so they pop. A CSS-driven segment has no render character to mismatch and no seam to hold. Everything built on that law goes with it: PSNR seam calibration at 18-25 dB, ffmpeg boundary-frame extraction, the crossfade-as-insurance rule, the one-model-per-chain rule. The blob-fetch trick (fetch to Blob so video.seekable is never [0,0] on a host without byte-range support) is a real and hard-won fix for a problem that only exists when you are scrubbing video. The GOP-8 encode settings, the mobile 9:16 second chain, iOS muted-video priming, seek coalescing while the decoder is busy: all video-decoder problems. The entire Higgsfield/Monid/Seedance layer is paid per clip in USD and is disqualified outright. Two things must be refused rather than merely skipped. First, scrub-engine.js itself: it ships a complete house style — sky gradient, drifting particles, pill nav, brand mark, numbered eyebrow-title-body-tags copy block, right-hand route rail with hover labels — and any three briefs that mount it produce three pages that look like each other. It is the exact liability this repository has failed four times. Take the SEGMENTS model and lingerEase; never take the file. Second, the whole art-direction layer (clay diorama, isometric tilt-shift, fly-through camera, the camera-grammar table mapping industry to camera move) is appearance, and the grammar table is worse than appearance because it is a lookup from category to treatment, which is convergence written down as a feature. From Remotion, nothing textual is takeable and little is wanted: the scaffold, Studio, multi-scene Sequence structure, and video-layout.md's numbers (84px headline, 44px supporting text, 80/100px safe area at 1080px wide) are canvas-composition figures with no meaning on a page that reflows, and they would collide with the floor's own type and touch-target measures. The one idea worth having from it — a scene is a pure function of one number — is stated in technique two and owes it no words.

plan.motionVerdict: Correct scope limit, not a gap. Keep "one deliberate moment or none". Four reasons in order of weight: (1) our arm shipped zero motion and placed first, and the AI-tell-hunting judge listed it as a credit ("Zero animation, and a reduced-motion rule stated as a guard against later additions"); U, also static, placed third; no judge penalised either. (2) There is no room: 730 tokens for four obligations in a new file, against 9 tokens spare in REDESIGN after the five items above, and a new file costs its scenario every run. (3) floor/buy.md already forbids motion near money, and buy is the package's main scenario, so a scene model would be opened least where it is loudest. (4) The licence position is bad: remotion-skills has no licence and may not be copied at all, scroll-world is MIT and would need a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES line, neither builds websites, and scrub-engine.js ships a complete house style (sky gradient, drifting particles, pill nav, route rail) that would make any three briefs mounting it look alike. The smallest honest version is not a scene model at all: it is the inverse of a check we already run. verify.mjs already fails on animation that survives prefers-reduced-motion but cannot see a scroll-reveal page whose content stays at opacity 0 forever because the JavaScript was correctly disabled, which passes every motion check by being blank. That lives in scripts/verify.mjs at zero token cost, because verify.md's Release commands block already names verify.mjs as the thing that runs the render matrix and floor measures. Ship it report-only for one round with exclusions for closed details, [hidden], aria-hidden and skip links.
